Elena — thanks, got the PO and the questions. Looping in Kimberly (billing) and Karthik (legal/sales ops) to confirm operational feasibility. High level response below, we can follow up with a redline: 

- Invoicing entity: We can support issuing invoices to Medway Srl but need to confirm whether billing will be split across Redwood US and Redwood EMEA legal entities (this affects tax residency on invoices). Typical approach: Redwood issues invoices from the EMEA entity for EU customers; if Medway requires split invoices (e.g., portion to US entity), we can accommodate but that will require accounting work — please confirm if the PO needs to route to multiple invoice recipients.

- VAT / gross-up vs reverse charge: Our standard is to issue invoices net of VAT and rely on reverse-charge where applicable, but we can accommodate a gross-up on a case-by-case basis if contractually requested. Gross-up would change the commercials (we'd increase your invoice amounts to cover VAT) — for transparency we can add an appendix showing the gross-up calculation and an option to toggle reverse-charge vs grossed invoices at the time of invoicing.

- Net terms: Redwood typically offers Net 30 for self‑serve/standard order forms. For larger committed contracts we are flexible to Net 45 in exchange for a small onboarding credit; if Medway prefers Net 45 we can propose a 2% onboarding credit applied to the first invoice.

Next steps I propose: Kimberly creates a short "invoicing flow" appendix (who issues, entity, VAT treatment, delivery of evidence) and Karthik will produce a redline of the order form that: (a) references Medway Srl as invoice recipient, (b) includes VAT appendix with gross-up option, and (c) documents Net 30 vs Net 45 swap terms and credit.

Kimberly/Karthik — are you ok to draft the attachments and a redline by EOD tomorrow? If Medway confirms Net 45 + onboarding credit I'll flag procurement concessions for approval.

Thanks,
